# openlineage_client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/openlineage-client/0.0.4/target-redirect/openlineage_client/

## Expand description

Transport-agnostic [OpenLineage](https://openlineage.io) event model and emit client.

This crate owns the emission side of OpenLineage: the [ RunEvent](https://docs.rs/event/struct.RunEvent.html) model and
its typed facets, a pluggable

[sink, and a non-blocking](https://docs.rs/transport/trait.Transport.html)

`Transport`[that hands events to a background drain task. It has](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html)

`OpenLineageClient`**no DataFusion (or any engine) dependency**— engine integrations such as

[build on top of it, and so can any other emitter.](https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage)

`datafusion-openlineage`[§](https://docs.rs#the-transport-seam)The transport seam

How events are published is deliberately unspecified. The [ Transport](https://docs.rs/transport/trait.Transport.html) trait
is the only seam: an implementation might POST to a spec-compliant OpenLineage
REST endpoint, publish to a Kafka topic, or do anything else. The crate ships

[,](https://docs.rs/transport/struct.NoopTransport.html)

`NoopTransport`[, and — behind the](https://docs.rs/transport/struct.ConsoleTransport.html)

`ConsoleTransport``http` feature —
[, which posts to an (optionally authenticated) HTTP endpoint via](https://docs.rs/cloud/struct.CloudClientTransport.html)

`CloudClientTransport``olai-http`. To target something else, implement [.](https://docs.rs/transport/trait.Transport.html)

`Transport`[§](https://docs.rs#non-blocking-emission)Non-blocking emission

[ OpenLineageClient::emit](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.emit) never blocks and never applies back-pressure: it
hands the event to a bounded channel drained by a background task. If the
queue is full the event is dropped with a warning — lineage must never slow or
break the host workload. Call

[before exit to drain queued events and flush the transport.](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.shutdown)

`OpenLineageClient::shutdown`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use openlineage_client::{ConsoleTransport, OpenLineageClient};
let client = OpenLineageClient::new(Arc::new(ConsoleTransport));
client.emit(event);          // non-blocking
client.shutdown().await;     // drain + flush before exit
```
[§](https://docs.rs#environment)Environment

[ OpenLineageClient::from_env](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.from_env) and

[read the standard OpenLineage environment variables, so an integration can wire itself up from the environment the rest of the ecosystem already uses:](https://docs.rs/config/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html#method.from_env)

`OpenLineageConfig::from_env`| Variable | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENLINEAGE_URL` | `OpenLineageClient::from_env` | Base URL of the endpoint (unset → no-op client) |
| `OPENLINEAGE_ENDPOINT` | `OpenLineageClient::from_env` | Path appended to the URL (default `/api/v1/lineage`) |
| `OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY` | `OpenLineageClient::from_env` | Bearer token, if set |
| `OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE` | `OpenLineageConfig::from_env` | Default job namespace |
| `OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `OpenLineageConfig::from_env` | Per-request transport timeout |
| `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_ID`/`OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_*` | `LineageContext::from_env` | Parent run facet |

# openlineage-client 0.0.4 - Docs.rs

# openlineage_client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/openlineage_client/index.html

## Expand description

Transport-agnostic [OpenLineage](https://openlineage.io) event model and emit client.

This crate owns the emission side of OpenLineage: the [ RunEvent](https://docs.rs/event/struct.RunEvent.html) model and
its typed facets, a pluggable

[sink, and a non-blocking](https://docs.rs/transport/trait.Transport.html)

`Transport`[that hands events to a background drain task. It has](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html)

`OpenLineageClient`**no DataFusion (or any engine) dependency**— engine integrations such as

[build on top of it, and so can any other emitter.](https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage)

`datafusion-openlineage`[§](https://docs.rs#the-transport-seam)The transport seam

How events are published is deliberately unspecified. The [ Transport](https://docs.rs/transport/trait.Transport.html) trait
is the only seam: an implementation might POST to a spec-compliant OpenLineage
REST endpoint, publish to a Kafka topic, or do anything else. The crate ships

[,](https://docs.rs/transport/struct.NoopTransport.html)

`NoopTransport`[, and — behind the](https://docs.rs/transport/struct.ConsoleTransport.html)

`ConsoleTransport``http` feature —
[, which posts to an (optionally authenticated) HTTP endpoint via](https://docs.rs/cloud/struct.CloudClientTransport.html)

`CloudClientTransport``olai-http`. To target something else, implement [.](https://docs.rs/transport/trait.Transport.html)

`Transport`[§](https://docs.rs#non-blocking-emission)Non-blocking emission

[ OpenLineageClient::emit](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.emit) never blocks and never applies back-pressure: it
hands the event to a bounded channel drained by a background task. If the
queue is full the event is dropped with a warning — lineage must never slow or
break the host workload. Call

[before exit to drain queued events and flush the transport.](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.shutdown)

`OpenLineageClient::shutdown`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use openlineage_client::{ConsoleTransport, OpenLineageClient};
let client = OpenLineageClient::new(Arc::new(ConsoleTransport));
client.emit(event);          // non-blocking
client.shutdown().await;     // drain + flush before exit
```
[§](https://docs.rs#environment)Environment

[ OpenLineageClient::from_env](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.from_env) and

[read the standard OpenLineage environment variables, so an integration can wire itself up from the environment the rest of the ecosystem already uses:](https://docs.rs/config/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html#method.from_env)

`OpenLineageConfig::from_env`| Variable | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENLINEAGE_URL` | `OpenLineageClient::from_env` | Base URL of the endpoint (unset → no-op client) |
| `OPENLINEAGE_ENDPOINT` | `OpenLineageClient::from_env` | Path appended to the URL (default `/api/v1/lineage`) |
| `OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY` | `OpenLineageClient::from_env` | Bearer token, if set |
| `OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE` | `OpenLineageConfig::from_env` | Default job namespace |
| `OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `OpenLineageConfig::from_env` | Per-request transport timeout |
| `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_ID`/`OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_*` | `LineageContext::from_env` | Parent run facet |

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [client](https://docs.rs/client/index.html)
- The OpenLineage client: a non-blocking emit front-end over a `Transport`
- [cloud](https://docs.rs/cloud/index.html)
- Default HTTP transport backed by `olai_http::CloudClient`
- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Static configuration shared across emitted events.
- [context](https://docs.rs/context/index.html)
- Top-level orchestration context contributed per emitted run.
- [event](https://docs.rs/event/index.html)
- OpenLineage run-event envelope.
- [facets](https://docs.rs/facets/index.html)
- OpenLineage facet types.
- [naming](https://docs.rs/naming/index.html)
- OpenLineage dataset naming-spec mapping.
- [transport](https://docs.rs/transport/index.html)
- Pluggable sink for OpenLineage events.

# lib.rs - source

# openlineage_client/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Transport-agnostic [OpenLineage](https://openlineage.io) event model and emit client.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! This crate owns the emission side of OpenLineage: the [`RunEvent`] model and
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! its typed facets, a pluggable [`Transport`] sink, and a non-blocking
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! [`OpenLineageClient`] that hands events to a background drain task. It has
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! **no DataFusion (or any engine) dependency** — engine integrations such as
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! [`datafusion-openlineage`](https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage) build on
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! top of it, and so can any other emitter.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! # The transport seam
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! How events are published is deliberately unspecified. The [`Transport`] trait
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! is the only seam: an implementation might POST to a spec-compliant OpenLineage
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! REST endpoint, publish to a Kafka topic, or do anything else. The crate ships
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! [`NoopTransport`], [`ConsoleTransport`], and — behind the `http` feature —
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! [`CloudClientTransport`], which posts to an (optionally authenticated) HTTP
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! endpoint via `olai-http`. To target something else, implement [`Transport`].
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! # Non-blocking emission
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! [`OpenLineageClient::emit`] never blocks and never applies back-pressure: it
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! hands the event to a bounded channel drained by a background task. If the
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! queue is full the event is dropped with a warning — lineage must never slow or
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! break the host workload. Call [`OpenLineageClient::shutdown`] before exit to
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! drain queued events and flush the transport.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! # Example
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! ```no_run
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! use std::sync::Arc;
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! use openlineage_client::{ConsoleTransport, OpenLineageClient};
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! # async fn run(event: openlineage_client::RunEvent) {
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! let client = OpenLineageClient::new(Arc::new(ConsoleTransport));
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! client.emit(event);          // non-blocking
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! client.shutdown().await;     // drain + flush before exit
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! # }
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! ```
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! # Environment
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! [`OpenLineageClient::from_env`] and [`OpenLineageConfig::from_env`] read the
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! standard OpenLineage environment variables, so an integration can wire itself
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! up from the environment the rest of the ecosystem already uses:
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! | Variable | Read by | Meaning |
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! |---|---|---|
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! | `OPENLINEAGE_URL` | [`OpenLineageClient::from_env`] | Base URL of the endpoint (unset → no-op client) |
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! | `OPENLINEAGE_ENDPOINT` | [`OpenLineageClient::from_env`] | Path appended to the URL (default `/api/v1/lineage`) |
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! | `OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY` | [`OpenLineageClient::from_env`] | Bearer token, if set |
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! | `OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE` | [`OpenLineageConfig::from_env`] | Default job namespace |
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! | `OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` | [`OpenLineageConfig::from_env`] | Per-request transport timeout |
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! | `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_ID` / `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_*` | [`LineageContext::from_env`] | Parent run facet |
[54](https://docs.rs#54)#![deny(missing_docs)]
[55](https://docs.rs#55)
[56](https://docs.rs#56)pub mod client;
[57](https://docs.rs#57)pub mod config;

[flush](https://docs.rs#method.flush)<'life0, 'async_trait>(
        &'life0 self,
    ) -> [Pin](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/pin/struct.Pin.html)<[Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/future/future/trait.Future.html)<Output = [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [TransportError](https://docs.rs/enum.TransportError.html)>> + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 'async_trait>>
       where Self: 'async_trait,
             'life0: 'async_trait { ... }
}## Expand description

A sink that delivers OpenLineage events to a backend.

The only required method is [ emit](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html#tymethod.emit).

[and](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html#method.emit_batch)

`emit_batch`[have default implementations; override them when the backend can deliver events in bulk or buffers internally.](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html#method.flush)

`flush`Implementations must never apply back-pressure that could stall the host workload — emission happens on a background drain task, but a transport that blocks indefinitely (e.g. on a hung upstream) can still starve every queued event. Bound your own IO with a timeout.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

    Self: 'async_trait,

#### fn [emit_batch](https://docs.rs#method.emit_batch)<'life0, 'life1, 'async_trait>(

    Self: 'async_trait,
    'life0: 'async_trait,
    'life1: 'async_trait,

Delivers a batch of events. The default implementation calls
[ emit](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html#tymethod.emit) for each event in order, stopping at the first
error. Override when the backend has a bulk endpoint (e.g. a batch POST).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

Returns a [ TransportError](https://docs.rs/enum.TransportError.html) if any event cannot be serialized or
delivered.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/openlineage_client/transport.rs.html#62-64)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/openlineage_client/transport.rs.html#62-64)

Flushes any internally-buffered events, blocking until they are delivered
(or fail). Called by [ OpenLineageClient::shutdown](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.shutdown)
after the drain queue empties. The default is a no-op — override it only
for transports that buffer beyond a single

[call.](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html#tymethod.emit)

`emit`[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

Returns a [ TransportError](https://docs.rs/enum.TransportError.html) if buffered events cannot be delivered.

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

#### pub fn [from_env](https://docs.rs#method.from_env)() -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [ClientError](https://docs.rs/enum.ClientError.html)>

Construct from the standard OpenLineage environment.

If `OPENLINEAGE_URL` is set, builds an HTTP transport (requires the
`http` feature); otherwise returns a no-op client. `OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY`,
if present, is sent as a bearer token.

Emit an event without blocking. On a full queue the event is dropped with a warning — lineage never applies back-pressure to the query.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/openlineage_client/client.rs.html#204-206)#### pub fn [dropped_count](https://docs.rs#method.dropped_count)(&self) -> [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/openlineage_client/client.rs.html#204-206)

#### pub fn [dropped_count](https://docs.rs#method.dropped_count)(&self) -> [u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)

Total events dropped so far — on a full/closed queue (back-pressure) or by transport failure. Process-global (shared across clones).

Flush queued events, flush the transport, and stop the background drain task.

Awaits the drain task to completion so events still queued at process exit
are delivered rather than lost, then calls [ Transport::flush](https://docs.rs/transport/trait.Transport.html#method.flush) so a
transport that buffers internally (e.g. a Kafka producer) delivers its
tail before exit. The drain task ends once the event channel closes, which
requires every sender to be dropped — so call this after (or while)
dropping all other clones of the client; this consumes the clone it is
called on. Idempotent across clones: only the clone holding the drain
handle awaits it, the rest return immediately.

# datafusion_openlineage - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/datafusion-openlineage

## Expand description

OpenLineage integration for Apache DataFusion.

Instrument a [ SessionState](https://docs.rs/datafusion/54.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/datafusion/execution/session_state/struct.SessionState.html)
with

[to emit](https://docs.rs/session/struct.OpenLineage.html#method.builder)

`OpenLineage::builder`[OpenLineage](https://openlineage.io)run events (START / COMPLETE / FAIL) describing each query’s input/output datasets and column-level lineage. Planning-time work (lineage extraction, context, START) runs in a

[; the terminal COMPLETE/FAIL node is installed by a registered](https://docs.rs/rule/struct.OpenLineageQueryPlanner.html)

`QueryPlanner`[that lowers a plan-carried marker — see the](https://docs.rs/rule/struct.LineageExtensionPlanner.html)

`ExtensionPlanner`[module and ADR 0005.](https://docs.rs/rule/index.html)

`rule`The event model, the pluggable [ Transport](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html) seam, and the non-blocking

[live in the engine-agnostic](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageClient.html)

`OpenLineageClient`[crate; this crate re-exports them and adds the DataFusion-specific glue. Orchestration metadata (parent run, job ids, custom facets) is injected per query via a](https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/openlineage_client/index.html)

`openlineage_client`[.](https://docs.rs/context/trait.LineageContextProvider.html)

`LineageContextProvider`[§](https://docs.rs#quickstart)Quickstart

```
use datafusion::execution::SessionStateBuilder;
use datafusion_openlineage::OpenLineage;
let state = SessionStateBuilder::new_with_default_features().build();
// Reads OPENLINEAGE_URL / _API_KEY / _NAMESPACE / parent-run env vars.
let state = OpenLineage::builder().from_env()?.instrument(state);
```

# CloudClientTransport in openlineage_client::cloud - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/openlineage_client/cloud/struct.CloudClientTransport.html

`pub struct CloudClientTransport { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Posts OpenLineage events to an HTTP endpoint via [ CloudClient](https://docs.rs/olai-http/0.0.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/olai_http/struct.CloudClient.html).

Single events go to `endpoint`; batches go to `batch_endpoint` (by default the
single endpoint with `/batch` appended, matching the OpenLineage HTTP API).

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# OpenLineageConfig in openlineage_client::config - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/openlineage-client/0.0.4/openlineage_client/config/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html

```
pub struct OpenLineageConfig {
    pub producer:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub job_namespace: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub engine_name: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub engine_version: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub adapter_version: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub request_timeout: [Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html),
}## Expand description

Identifies the emitting integration on every emitted event/facet, and tunes the emit transport.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.producer)

`producer: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)`producer` URI stamped on events and facets (the emitting code). Engine
integrations should override this with their own identity.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.job_namespace)

`job_namespace: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Default job namespace when the context provides none
(from `OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE`, falling back to `"default"`).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.engine_name)

`engine_name: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Engine name for the `processing_engine` run facet. Empty unless an engine
integration sets it.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.engine_version)

`engine_version: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Engine version for the `processing_engine` run facet. Empty unless an
engine integration sets it.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.adapter_version)

`adapter_version: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)This crate’s version, for `openlineageAdapterVersion`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.request_timeout)

`request_timeout: `[Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html)Per-request timeout applied by HTTP transports. One slow/hung upstream
request can otherwise stall the shared background drain; bounding it lets
the drain keep making progress. See `OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Build a config from the standard OpenLineage environment conventions.

Reads `OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE` for the default job namespace (falling back
to [ DEFAULT_NAMESPACE](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.html)) and

`OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` for the request
timeout (falling back to [); the producer/adapter identity is fixed for this crate and the engine identity is left empty (an engine integration such as](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.html)

`DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT``datafusion-openlineage` stamps it). This is
the documented entry point for env-driven configuration — pair it with
[, which reads](https://docs.rs/client/struct.OpenLineageClient.html#method.from_env)

`OpenLineageClient::from_env``OPENLINEAGE_URL` / `OPENLINEAGE_ENDPOINT` / `OPENLINEAGE_API_KEY`
for the transport, so an integration can wire itself up entirely from the
environment the rest of the OpenLineage ecosystem already uses.[ Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) is equivalent and reads the same environment;

`from_env`
exists to make the env dependency explicit and discoverable at call sites.[ Self::from_env](https://docs.rs/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html#method.from_env) with the

`OPENLINEAGE_NAMESPACE` / `OPENLINEAGE_TIMEOUT_MS`
values injected, so the fallback logic is unit-testable without mutating
process-global env. An absent or empty namespace falls back to
[; an absent/empty/unparsable timeout falls back to](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_NAMESPACE.html)

`DEFAULT_NAMESPACE`[.](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.html)

`DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/openlineage_client/context.rs.html#47-53)#### pub fn [from_env](https://docs.rs#method.from_env)(config: &[OpenLineageConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/openlineage_client/context.rs.html#47-53)

#### pub fn [from_env](https://docs.rs#method.from_env)(config: &[OpenLineageConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.OpenLineageConfig.html)) -> Self

Build a context from the established OpenLineage parent-run environment
conventions, returning `None`-filled fields when nothing is set.

Reads `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_ID` (slash form `{namespace}/{name}/{runId}`),
falling back to the discrete `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_JOB_NAMESPACE` /
`OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_JOB_NAME` / `OPENLINEAGE_PARENT_RUN_ID` variables.

pub enum ClientError {
    Config(
```

}## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Config)

### Config([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))

The client could not be built from the given configuration or environment — for example, no Tokio runtime was available to host the drain task, or an endpoint URL was malformed.
